items.title: Joe Harris Interview, 1961-04-12
items.q: And from the tuxedo club I went to the Budweiser with Artie.

ctx.x: Had he been around in New Orleans long or did you work with him mostly traveling around

outside? No, I tell you, we picked him up in Monroe, Louisiana. He was traveling with a little band out of Monroe. And the Celestan band was playing at night. They had a club over there on De Hennessy Street, I think it is. He called it the Savoy. Well, this was an opening night that night and we had the job to open it up. That's the time when Anderson was making all those high notes and they wanted to write the ripplet. He was the first to make all those high notes on the trumpets, you know? And that's when we…

The last time I saw the big chief, as they call him, Moore, he was at the famous door. He stopped in to see some of the musicians. I think Santa Picora and others he knew. And I was surprised they all knew him. I'd never known he'd been down this part of the country at that time.
